title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-improved-errors-and-openai-compat
author: Avery Kim
description: Add JSONSchema 'strict' validation mode with improved error messages and integrate behavior with the OpenAI compatibility layer. Motivation: users relying on structured output frequently run into ambiguous validation errors when responses partially match schemas; strict mode enforces exact schema conformance and returns actionable, stable error payloads for downstream tooling and function/tool-calling flows. This PR: - introduces a configurable response_format.strict boolean flag that triggers schema-first validation and deterministic error shaping; - adds richer validation error codes (MISSING_FIELD, TYPE_MISMATCH, EXTRA_FIELD, ENUM_MISMATCH, INVALID_FORMAT) and path-based locations; - surfaces structured error payloads via the OpenAI compatibility adapter so third-party clients see compatible error semantics; - preserves streaming when possible: the runtime performs optimistic streaming and validates final fragments, sending a final validation frame if strict mode fails; - adds fallback policies and automatic gentle mode: customers can opt to return non-strict best-effort outputs plus a validation warning instead of hard failure; - includes migration notes, docs updates, unit and integration tests, and observability events for validation failures. Related Linear: ENG-2142, PM-934. Checklist: - [x] API and adapter implementation - [x] unit tests for validator and error shaping - [x] integration tests for streaming + strict validation - [x] docs and migration guidance - [x] release notes and runtime metrics emission

summary_of_changes: Adds response_format.strict flag and strict-mode validator, improves validation error schema and mapping to OpenAI-compatible error payloads, ensures streaming remains stable with final validation frames, and ships tests and docs.
review_conversation: Reviewer Nina: please clarify whether strict mode is opt-in or opt-out and how this interacts with existing function/tool calling. Author: strict mode is opt-in by default; console and API can set response_format.strict=true per-request or via model route. Reviewer Marco: validation payload shape looks good, but we should avoid leaking internal field names in errors; request change. Author: sanitized error paths and added a canonical field mapping layer. Reviewer Janelle: can we emit a metric for validation_failures with schema_id and failure_code? Author: added metrics emission and unit tests. Final: Approved by Nina and Marco; Janelle approved after metrics were added.
release_notes:
- Introduce response_format.strict: opt-in strict JSONSchema validation mode with explicit error codes and OpenAI-compatible error mapping.
- Improved validation error messages and observability for structured-output workloads.
- Streaming behavior: optimistic streaming preserved; final validation frame emitted on strict failures.
Migration: existing routes are unchanged unless response_format.strict is enabled. Review the migration guidance in docs/response_formats.md.
migration_guidance: Strict mode is opt-in. To enable: set response_format.strict=true on the route or per-request. If you previously relied on best-effort parsing, enable gentle_mode to receive validation warnings instead of hard failures. See redwood/docs/response_formats.md for examples and a recommended rollout plan (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
tests: Added unit tests for jsonschema_validator error codes and serializers, integration tests for streaming + strict validation, and OpenAI compatibility adapter tests that assert the external payload shape. CI run includes full unit, integration, and lint. Local fuzzing used example prompts from existing structured-output harness.
changelog_entry: Added strict JSONSchema response validation with improved, OpenAI-compatible error payloads and streaming-safe final validation frames. Opt-in via response_format.strict.
